Your run uses dt=0.03 → diffusion number r = αdt/dx² = **0.30 > 0.25**. The old dt=0.02 gave r=0.20 (stable, 20 % margin). The checkerboard you see is the signature: the odd/even mode has amplification **1 − 8r = −1.40** at dt=0.03 (sign-flipping, growing 40 %/step), **−1.00** at dt=0.025 (marginal, never decays), **−0.60** at dt=0.02 (decays). I reproduced all three regimes numerically.

One anomaly I could not explain from the stated cause: between steps 250 (3.3e21) and 262 (NaN) your log grows by ~10²⁴ per step, while no linear operator with r=0.3 can exceed 1.4 per step — so something else (decimated step counter, varying dt, or a solver/normalisation path) is involved in the last 12 steps.
